message.content: {"caption":"A three-stage knowledge-incorporation workflow uses an Apollo passage to generate a self-edit, fine-tunes the model, and answers an evaluation question correctly.","description":"A horizontal workflow on a light-gray rounded panel is headed “Knowledge Incorporation Setup” and divided into “Passage,” “Self-Edit,” and “Evaluation.” In Passage, the text reads “title: Apollo program” and “context: But even after NASA reached internal agreement, it was far from smooth sailing...” with a blue bar beneath it. A right-pointing arrow leads to a boxed “LM” containing an orange parameter tile labeled θ_t, followed by another right-pointing arrow to the Self-Edit text: “1. The Apollo program faced opposition from Kennedy’s science advisor, Jerome Wiesner, who had...” A yellow bar is beneath this text. A right-pointing arrow leads to an “SFT” box; an upward arrow from SFT points to an orange updated-parameter tile labeled θ′_t above it. In Evaluation, the question “Who was Kennedy’s science adviser that opposed manned spacecraft flights?” appears above a blue bar. A right-pointing arrow leads to a boxed “LM” with an orange θ′_t tile, then another right-pointing arrow leads to the answer “Jerome Wiesner,” underlined in blue. A check mark above the answer indicates it is correct.","figure_type":"diagram","chart_values":[]}
